description: Corrections from the citation sweep of the 125 approved questions (docs/question-verify/approved-bank-findings.md). Every op is a targeted PATCH to a known value, so reruns are no-ops.

ops.why: Premise is foreign signage: there is no blue rectangular pedestrian-crossing sign in South Africa. Schedule 1 R5 is a RED sign for a pedestrian PRECINCT, which the project's own chart verification records (data/verify/verdicts/R5.json: 'red diamond … white walking-pedestrian symbol') and the road_signs row confirms ('Pedestrian priority zone'). The blue square is the Vienna Convention sign. Cannot be fixed by citation, so the row is withdrawn rather than deleted — draft removes it from the exam pool, the readiness set AND practice (getPracticeQuestions filters on review_status alone, so in_exam=false is not enough on its own).

Question asks about a black '80' in a red-bordered circle but rendered R201-60 ('Speed limit of 60 km/h') above the prompt. R201-80 exists, is approved on both gates, and has public/signs/R201-80.svg.

Question describes 'a red-bordered triangle showing an inverted T' but rendered W409, which is the T-junction CHEVRON board, not a triangle. W104 is the square-on T: chart verification records 'a horizontal top bar with a vertical stem descending from its centre'. NOT W105/W106 — those are the skew variants (bar angled high-left and high-right respectively), so an 'inverted T' stem does not describe them.

Question describes 'a triangle with edges angling inward' warning the road narrows, but rendered W214 ('Right lane ends ahead' — an up-arrow with a second arrow merging from the right). W328 is 'Roadway narrows from both sides ahead', whose chart glyph is exactly both edges tapering inward symmetrically.

Worst of the four: the question asks which sign shows a car with curved skid marks, and rendered W325 (gravel road begins) — which is option 0, one of its own distractors. W333 is 'Slippery road ahead' ('a car above S-shaped skid marks'). Root cause is upstream: the wiki note's related_signs lists the DISTRACTOR ('Gravel Road Sign'), not the sign under test.

set.explanation: A learner's licence does not permit driving alone. Regulation 99(2)(a) requires you to be under the direct personal supervision of someone seated next to you who holds a full licence for that class of vehicle. There is no L-plate requirement in South African law.

ops.why: Two defects. (1) The explanation asserted the learner 'must display L plates'. There is no L-plate requirement anywhere in the Act or the Regulations — reg 99(2) lists exactly three conditions on a learner's licence (supervision, no motorcycle passenger, no carrying persons for reward). It is UK law. (2) The keyed answer says you must ALWAYS be supervised, but reg 99(2)(a) exempts 'a motor vehicle having no seating accommodation for a passenger or … a motor cycle' — so the keyed answer was false for a Code A learner. Dropping A from vehicle_codes scopes the item to the vehicles the rule actually governs.

set.explanation: Towing a trailer over 750 kg behind a light motor vehicle requires Code EB. Code A is for motorcycles; Code C is a bus or goods vehicle whose gross vehicle mass exceeds 16 000 kg — the 3 500 kg to 16 000 kg band is Code C1.

ops.why: The explanation said 'Code C is for heavy vehicles over 3 500 kg'. The reg 100 code table defines C as 'a bus or a goods vehicle, the gross vehicle mass of which exceeds 16 000 kilograms'; 'exceeds 3 500 kilograms but does not exceed 16 000 kilograms' is C1. A learner who memorised this fails a C1 question. The keyed answer (EB) is correct and unchanged.

set.explanation: A time-based gap (the two-second rule) is correct because the safe distance grows automatically with speed. A fixed metre distance or 'one car length' does not scale with speed and is unsafe at higher speeds.

set.explanation: The foot (service) brake is the control for stopping quickly. The handbrake holds a stationary vehicle, and although regulation 149 allows it to double as the emergency brake if the service brake fails, it is not how you make an emergency stop. The clutch disengages the engine from the wheels and does not brake at all.

ops.why: The explanation said the handbrake 'only keeps a stationary vehicle still'. Reg 149's proviso (a) reads 'the emergency brake and parking brake may be one and the same brake', and reg 1 defines an emergency brake as 'a brake, other than a service brake, which can stop a vehicle' — so in law the handbrake may well BE the emergency brake. Settled by John 2026-07-30: 'Yes they are one and the same'. The keyed answer (foot brake) was always right; the reasoning given for it was not.

set.explanation: Fasten before the vehicle moves off. Regulation 213(4) requires an adult occupying a seat that is fitted with a seatbelt to wear it, and the only exception is while reversing or moving in or out of a parking bay. Belts are not optional on short trips and not limited to the open road.

ops.why: The explanation claimed belts must be worn 'at all times', which is wider than the regulation. Reg 213(4) carries an express proviso: 'the provisions of this regulation do not apply while reversing or moving in or out of a parking bay or area'. Confirmed by John 2026-07-30: the requirement drops during low-speed parking-area movements and reversing. The keyed answer ('before the vehicle moves off') is unchanged.

options: An automatic still needs a clutch pedal for each gear change
An automatic has no clutch pedal and selects gears itself
An automatic has no gears at all
set.explanation: An automatic has no clutch pedal and selects its own gears; the driver only moves the selector (P/R/N/D). There is no clutch for the driver to operate, and the vehicle does have gears.

ops.why: The defect was in the keyed OPTION text, not the explanation: it read 'An automatic has no clutch', which is mechanically false — a torque-converter automatic contains clutch packs and a DCT has two. The explanation already said 'no clutch CONTROL', so option and explanation contradicted each other. Settled by John 2026-07-30: 'Yes Automatic has no clutch (clutch control)'. Both options now say 'clutch pedal' so the contrast stays clean; answer index 1 is unchanged.

set.explanation: The motorcycle front brake is operated by the right-hand lever. Stopping uses front and rear brakes together.

ops.why: The keyed answer holds for every motorcycle — the right lever is always the front brake — but the explanation went on to say 'the rear brake is the right-foot pedal and the clutch is the left-hand lever'. That is false for a twist-and-go scooter, which has no clutch lever and no foot brake pedal: its LEFT lever is the rear brake. The item is scoped vehicle_codes {A}, which covers scooters, so a scooter learner was being taught that the left lever is the clutch when on their machine it is a brake. John chose option (b) on 2026-07-30: delete the clause rather than scope it, since it is not needed to explain the answer.

The item asks which control changes the vehicle's direction and answers 'the steering wheel', while scoped {A,B,C,EB} — a motorcycle has handlebars, so for a Code A learner the keyed answer named a control not on the vehicle. Same defect as RR-019. Dropped A rather than rewording to 'steering wheel or handlebars' because objective VC1 is car-only prose ('Steers the car', 'quarter to three', 'both hands on the wheel') and there is no handlebar learning object — the motorcycle series VC18-VC22 covers throttle, both brakes, clutch and stopping, but not steering. Rewording would have kept the mismatch and merely moved it to the lesson the learner is sent to. A motorcycle steering question can be added later once an objective exists for it.
